plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing auctions you could have profitably won. With a value of $31, bidding exactly $31 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable and never overpay.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $22 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. This maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This is because the payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding your true value maximizes expected profit—bidding higher risks overpaying, bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. With my value at $40, I should bid exactly $40 to ensure I win whenever it's profitable and pay only the second-highest bid.
